759	// isStartTimestampReset tells whether there was a counter reset by checking the start timestamp value.
760	func isStartTimestampReset(prevStartTimestamp, prevTimestamp, currStartTimestamp, currTimestamp int64) bool {
761		if prevStartTimestamp == currStartTimestamp || currStartTimestamp == 0 || currStartTimestamp >= currTimestamp {
762			// No reset if start timestamp hasn't changed, if it is not set (value is 0), if it is clearly invalid
763			// (ST > T), or if it is OTel's unknown start time (ST == T).
764			return false
765		}
766	
767		if currStartTimestamp < prevTimestamp {
768			return false
769		}
770	
771		if currStartTimestamp > prevTimestamp {
772			return true
773		}
774	
775		// If this place is reached, then it means that the current datapoint start timestamp is pointing
776		// to a previous datapoint. In OTel, this should only happen in two cases:
777		// * this is a delta series,
778		// * or this is a cumulative series with unknown start timestamp.
779		//
780		// This should be treated as a reset for deltas, but it is not a reset for cumulative series
781		// with unknown start timestamp. Thus we have to check whether the start timestamp
782		// of the previous datapoint is known.
783		//
784		// A previous start timestamp greater than the previous sample timestamp is invalid; treat it
785		// as unknown to avoid a spurious reset.
786		if prevStartTimestamp > prevTimestamp {
787			return false
788		}
789		return prevStartTimestamp != 0 && prevStartTimestamp != prevTimestamp
790	}
791	
792	// checkStartTimeOverlap detects when a sample's start timestamp overlaps with a
793	// previous sample's timestamp, indicating potential data quality issues.
794	// Works for both delta and cumulative counter metrics.
795	//
796	// Returns true when: currST != 0 && currST < prevT && currST != prevST
797	// This correctly handles:
798	//   - Valid deltas: currST = prevT (no overlap detected)
799	//   - Valid cumulative: currST = prevST (no overlap detected)
800	//   - Invalid overlap: currST < prevT && currST != prevST (overlap detected)
801	func checkStartTimeOverlap(prevStartTimestamp, prevTimestamp, currStartTimestamp int64) bool {
802		return currStartTimestamp != 0 && currStartTimestamp < prevTimestamp && currStartTimestamp != prevStartTimestamp
803	}
